courses.title: Discrete Structures

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Computer Architecture
courses.description: Fundamentals of computer architecture: digital logic design, working up through processor design, pipelining, and memory hierarchy.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: System Programming
courses.description: Introduction to system programming: processes, threads, synchronization, networking, filesystems, and signals, taught through extensive C programming.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Numerical Methods I
courses.description: Fundamentals of numerical methods: floating point, solving linear and nonlinear equations, interpolation, differentiation, integration, and least squares.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Probability & Statistics for Computer Science
courses.description: Introduction to probability and statistics with applications in computing: random variables, distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing, and regression.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Introduction to Algorithms & Models of Computation
courses.description: Analysis of algorithms, NP-completeness, automata theory, formal languages, and computability.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Database Systems
courses.description: Organization and management of database systems: relational model, SQL, design theory, query processing, and transactions.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Distributed Systems
courses.description: Key concepts in distributed systems: time and ordering, consensus, replication, fault tolerance, and large-scale system design case studies.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Artificial Intelligence
courses.description: Major topics in artificial intelligence: search, knowledge representation, reasoning, machine learning foundations, and natural language processing.

courses.subject: CS
courses.title: Special Topics: Coding Studio
courses.description: Eight-week studio topics course (first half of term): collaborative software projects and code review practice.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Logic and Reasoning
courses.description: Eight-week course (second half of term) on deductive logic: validity, soundness, proof, and common fallacies. Fulfills Quantitative Reasoning.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Introduction to Computing
courses.description: Introduction to digital logic, computer systems, and C programming for electrical and computer engineering students.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Computer Systems & Programming
courses.description: Advanced use of assembly language and C: subroutines, stacks, interrupts, device drivers, and introductory operating systems concepts.

courses.subject: ECE
courses.title: Digital Systems Laboratory
courses.description: Design and implementation of digital systems using SystemVerilog and FPGA hardware, culminating in a final project.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: First course in calculus and analytic geometry: limits, derivatives, and integrals with applications.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus II
courses.description: Second course in calculus: techniques of integration, series, parametric equations, and polar coordinates.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Calculus III
courses.description: Third course in calculus: vectors, partial derivatives, multiple integrals, and vector calculus theorems.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Linear Algebra with Computational Applications
courses.description: Linear algebra with a computational focus: matrices, vector spaces, eigenvalues, and numerical methods in Python.

courses.subject: MATH
courses.title: Fundamental Mathematics
courses.description: Introduction to proof: logic, sets, functions, number theory, and combinatorics. Prepares students for advanced mathematics courses.

courses.subject: STAT
courses.title: Statistical Analysis
courses.description: Survey of statistical concepts and reasoning: descriptive statistics, probability, inference, and regression, with computer analysis.

courses.subject: STAT
courses.title: Statistics and Probability I
courses.description: Introduction to mathematical statistics and probability: distributions, expectation, estimation, and hypothesis testing.

courses.subject: PHIL
courses.title: Introduction to Philosophy
courses.description: Introduction to the central problems of philosophy: knowledge, reality, mind, freedom, and the meaning of life, through classic and contemporary readings.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Microeconomic Principles
courses.description: Introduction to the microeconomic analysis of markets: supply and demand, consumer and firm behavior, and market structures.

courses.subject: ECON
courses.title: Macroeconomic Principles
courses.description: Introduction to macroeconomic analysis: national income, inflation, unemployment, monetary and fiscal policy.

courses.subject: PSYC
courses.title: Intro Psych
courses.description: Study of human and animal behavior and mental processes: perception, learning, memory, thinking, personality, and social behavior.

courses.subject: HIST
courses.title: US History Since 1877
courses.description: Survey of United States history from Reconstruction to the present: industrialization, world wars, civil rights, and globalization.

courses.subject: ANTH
courses.title: Anthro in a Changing World
courses.description: Introduction to cultural anthropology: culture, kinship, language, religion, and globalization studied through ethnographic cases.

courses.subject: RHET
courses.title: Writing and Research
courses.description: Instruction and practice in expository writing and research: composing arguments, evaluating sources, and academic citation.

courses.subject: BADM
courses.title: Principles of Marketing
courses.description: Introduction to marketing strategy and management: consumer behavior, segmentation, product, pricing, promotion, and distribution. Evening online synchronous section.
